name: React Three Fiber
role: React renderer for Three.js: declarative JSX scenes with hooks for the frame loop
summary: React reconciler that maps JSX to Three.js objects and exposes useFrame, useThree and an event system. Output is the same canvas as plain Three.js. Distinguishing strength: declarative scene composition and the pmndrs component ecosystem. Majors are tied to React: v9 targets React 19, v8 React 18.
use_when: Over plain Three.js when scenes are React components with props and state
With drei and postprocessing for shots composed from reusable pieces
Seek-driven frames through frameloop never and advance
avoid_when: No React in the project: Three.js directly
Tight render-once-per-seek control: plain Three.js is simpler
Non-React engines wanted: Babylon.js or PlayCanvas

evidence.result: 90 frames at 1280x720, shuffled order matches sequential, distinct hashes, frame 45 alpha 0..1; react 19.3.1, three 0.186.1, esbuild 0.25.12, Playwright 1.64.1, Chromium 156.0.8078.4.
evidence.scope: R3F Canvas frameloop never, seek via flushSync state + advance, esbuild-bundled TSX; alpha; no events, useFrame clocks or loaded assets; repo-only, macOS arm64.

notes: 2026-10-26: frameloop never with advance() for seek-driven capture is from memory of the docs and was not verified.
2026-11-12: frameloop never with advance() verified in examples/react-capture; flushSync before advance was sufficient.

assessment.rationale: pmndrs maintained, release Oct 2026; v9 pairs with React 19. Adds a React layer to Three.js rather than a different renderer.
